lesson.title: The Big Hitter: Time for You, Not Them
lesson.hook: Their ball arrives fast and heavy. Win back your time, and keep the ball out of their favourite height.
lesson.memHTML: Take a step back. Keep it out of their zone.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time someone hits big, take one step back before the rally starts and notice how much time it gives you.

pro.label: Moutet's slice against bigger hitters
pro.moment: The ATP Tour's TopCourt piece with Moutet shows how he keeps his backhand slice low and angling away to neutralise bigger hitters, turning a game of power into a game of chess.
pro.read: Pace needs a ball at the right height. Don't give it to them.

drill.name: Out of the zone
drill.how: Your partner feeds hard, deep balls. Start one big step behind the baseline. Score a point for every reply that reaches them below the knee or above the shoulder, and lose one for every ball that sits at their waist.

lesson.cue: Step back. Keep it out of their zone.

steps.name: Their big ball
steps.sit: They hit big. Their crosscourt forehand is coming into your backhand corner at 125 km/h.
steps.q: Where do you wait for it?
steps.payoff: One big step back gives you about twice the time of your usual spot.
steps.principle: Against pace, buy time with your feet first.
steps.why: Their ball covers the court so fast that your usual spot leaves a third of a second. One big step back lets it slow and drop, so you meet it with time to spare. Much further back, you have to come forward again.
steps.take: Facing a big hitter? Start one big step back.

lines.A: Way back, you have to come forward to meet it: 0.4 s to spare.
lines.B: Your usual spot: only a third of a second to spare.
lines.C: Right: one big step back gives you 0.6 s, about twice as long.
lines.D: Inside the baseline, their pace rushes you: 0.1 s to spare.

steps.name: What you send back
steps.sit: You're set, a step back. Their best shots come from a ball at waist to chest height.
steps.q: Which reply keeps their next ball small?
steps.payoff: Below their waist, they can't swing big.
steps.principle: Pace needs the right height. Don't give it to them.
steps.why: Deep through the middle and the heavy crosscourt both reach them waist high, their favourite height, and the big ball comes back. The low slice stays below their waist and takes long enough to get there that you're ready again.
steps.unlock: Keep it out of their zone
steps.take: Big hitter? Keep it out of their zone.

lines.A: Right: the slice stays below their waist. Rally pace back; you're in time.
lines.B: Deep middle sits at their waist: their big ball, and you're stretched.
lines.C: Flat and low works too, but it clears the net by 62 cm, the slice by 95.
lines.D: The heavy ball reaches them waist high: big ball back, just in time.

steps.name: Now to your forehand
steps.sit: Their big inside-out forehand is coming to your forehand. Choose where you wait and what you hit.
opts: Step back, high over their shoulder
Step back, deep through the middle
steps.payoff: Time first, then keep it out of their zone, this time over the top.
steps.principle: Low or high: anything but their waist.
steps.why: Stepping inside leaves you rushed, and a rushed ball lands short, where they step in and swing big. From a step back, a high ball reaches them above the shoulder, and their reply comes back at rally pace.
steps.take: Low slice or high ball: anything but their waist.

lines.A: Heavy and deep still reaches their waist: big ball back, just in time.
lines.B: Right: time first, then over their shoulder. Rally pace back; you're in time.
lines.C: Inside the baseline you're rushed; it lands short and their big ball wins.
lines.D: Deep middle sits at their waist: their big ball, and you're stretched.
